ideas.risks: The boundary defect may be large for algebraic reasons that do not imply a local market conflict; a false inequality here would likely be exposed by stable-singleton or alternating paths.
ideas.summary: Attack the solver's exact obstruction: replace the crude cross-scale boundary term m min(||u||_1,||v||_1) by an intrinsic defect term. For f_t(w)=sup_a a sum_T w_T 1{a<M_{t,T}}, study f_t(u)+f_t(v)-f_t(u+v) on t<m and try to prove that a large total boundary defect itself yields a finite-prefix D_m certificate. A target conditional inequality is: dual mass split across scales can only create large positive Phi if either one side already has positive Phi or the boundary prefix has D_m=Omega(m).
ideas.title: Boundary Defect Implies Local Conflict
ideas.why_promising: This directly addresses the gap in iteration 14. If true, recursive dyadic splitting would turn failure of a fixed sublinear envelope into comparable-scale finite-prefix certificates, proving D_n=o(n) suffices.

ideas.risks: Finite alphabets may still contain the full obstruction, or quantizing arbitrary paths may destroy the strict-crossing/left-limit structure needed for a general theorem.
ideas.summary: Restrict first to paths with prices in a fixed finite alphabet 0<p_1<...<p_k. Rewrite the dual using last-exceedance functions L_j(T)=max{s<=T:P_s>p_j}; the per-time dual term becomes max_j p_j sum_{T:t<L_j(T)} lambda_T. This is a nested interval/laminar structure. Try to prove an uncrossing theorem: any profitable dual certificate can be converted, up to lower-order loss, into one supported on a horizon window comparable to its affected prefix.
ideas.title: Finite-Alphabet Laminar Dual
ideas.why_promising: The last-exceedance representation is the most market-specific structure currently available. A finite-alphabet theorem would be a meaningful positive result and a plausible stepping stone to approximation.

ideas.risks: Repeated repairs may not converge, and cumulative future damage from repairing many prefixes may be linear at some horizons. The scalar D_n=o(n) hypothesis may be too weak to provide enough slack for intermediate horizons.
ideas.summary: Try to build the infinite marginal sequence directly by staged repairs. Given a good finite optimizer for a long prefix n and a shorter protected prefix m<<n, replace the first m marginals by ones that repair horizons <=m. Prefix-splicing says all later deficits change by at most m. Explore whether a schedule m_k<<n_k can make cumulative repair damage o(T), yielding a fixed sublinear envelope from D_n=o(n).
ideas.title: Staged Prefix Repair Construction
ideas.why_promising: This uses the accepted prefix-splicing robustness in the primal rather than fighting the dual. It may prove sufficiency without a full localization theorem.

ideas.risks: Finite-n artifacts may look like separators but vanish under extension; also E_n-type fixed-envelope proxies need to be chosen carefully to avoid merely restating D_n.
ideas.summary: Implement finite-prefix LP computations over small price alphabets and search for paths where D_m/m is small for every prefix m but a fixed-envelope proxy stays bounded away from zero. Useful proxies include inf_mu max_{T<=n} d_T/T, dyadic-weighted objectives, and constraints requiring d_T<=epsilon_T T for prescribed slowly vanishing epsilon_T. Search over non-block interleavings, nested separated blocks, and alternating low/high record patterns.
ideas.title: LP Search For A Market Separator
ideas.why_promising: A concrete finite counterexample pattern would focus the negative route; failure to find one across structured searches would give evidence for finite-alphabet gluing and identify invariants.

ideas.risks: The finite-prefix value may simply add the local kappa losses over many blocks and become linear, killing D_n=o(n). Conversely, a path-aware policy may adapt block by block and avoid global failure.
ideas.summary: Generalize the failed separated-block attempt from one diluted conflict to many diluted conflicts. Build paths with many small old conflicts, each o(T) at its later revealing horizon, but whose cumulative unresolved incompatibility might be Omega(T) for any fixed policy. Candidate forms are repeated 0^{N_i},c_0,0^{L_i},c_1 modules with alternating threshold roles or moving-scale equal-revenue menus. For each candidate, compute whether D_n adds local conflicts or remains diluted.
ideas.title: Cumulative Diluted Conflicts
ideas.why_promising: The simple separated block fails because one old conflict is diluted. A cumulative construction is the most plausible remaining negative route resembling the abstract parity obstruction while respecting fresh market coordinates.

ideas.risks: Approachability may only rederive the fixed-envelope compactness criterion, not the weaker scalar D_n condition. The game is nonstationary because horizon offsets V_T^* and active coordinates change with time.
ideas.summary: Formulate the known-path problem as simultaneous approachability of the negative orthant for horizon-indexed deficits. A quote distribution at time t contributes a vector to all coordinates T>t, while V_T^* supplies a fixed target offset. Use l_infinity or pseudonorm approachability duality to ask whether finite supported horizon-dual tests are enough for a uniform strategy, and compare the resulting condition to D_n and the fixed-envelope criterion.
ideas.title: Simultaneous-Horizon Approachability
ideas.why_promising: This may import mature machinery for one sequence serving many criteria and could clarify exactly which uniform condition is missing from D_n=o(n).

ideas.risks: Generic infinite-LP or uniform-value criteria may be too abstract and fail to exploit market suffix-max structure; the output may be only a conditional theorem.
ideas.summary: Look for a total-boundedness or tightness condition under which finite-prefix feasibility upgrades to fixed-envelope feasibility. Translate Renault-style total boundedness of value families or countably-infinite LP approximation conditions into this setting, perhaps as compactness of normalized last-exceedance profiles or moment bounds on bad dual horizon weights. Then test whether finite alphabets, record-stable paths, or bounded active-threshold paths satisfy it automatically.
ideas.title: Total-Boundedness Gluing Criterion
ideas.why_promising: Even if D_n=o(n) alone remains open, a clean intermediate condition could be the right structural theorem and would explain why generic compactness is insufficient.

ideas.risks: The calculations may become case-heavy and only confirm dilution rather than producing a theorem. For m>2, strict left-limit and intermediate-horizon corrections need careful handling.
ideas.summary: Finish and generalize the separated-block calculation. Compute D_n exactly, or within o(n), for paths of the form 0^{N_0},c_0,0^{N_1},c_1,...,0^{N_k},c_k with increasing thresholds and varying gaps. Determine whether the finite-prefix value is a max of active local conflicts, a sum, or a more subtle convolution. Use these formulas as regression tests for both localization and separator attempts.
ideas.title: Separated Multi-Block Formula
ideas.why_promising: Iteration 14's exact two-threshold separated block explains one failed counterexample. A general formula would sharply delimit which block constructions can or cannot separate D_n=o(n) from fixed-envelope feasibility.
